title: The Impact of Frozen Storage of Raw Material Prior to Processing on the Safety and Quality of the Salted Anchovies (Engraulis encrasicolus, Linnaeus, 1758) Under Ambient Temperatures
content: Despite being commonly marketed as frozen, the market value of frozen anchovies falls at the start of the new fishing season and is usually used as animal feed. Therefore, it is possible to utilize long-term frozen anchovies as salted products. Thus, this study investigates the effect of frozen storage of anchovies prior to salting on the quality changes and food safety under ambient conditions. Two groups of fresh anchovies were created as (i) the control group consisting of anchovies freshly processed without freezing/ frozen storage, and (ii) the experimental group of frozen anchovies at -18°C for one year. Anchovies were salted using dry-salting and brining (with 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30% salt concentrations). Results demonstrated that the variation in salt concentrations and salting methods affected the safety and quality of the salted anchovies (p&lt;0.05). Freezing/frozen storage anchovies before salting improved the shelf-life of salted anchovies, with the highest shelf-life was observed for dry-salted anchovies in the experimental group as 10 months. Strong correlations were observed between organoleptic scores and chemical quality parameters (R2: 0.87-0.99 for control and 0.86-0.99 for experimental). The overall results suggest that frozen anchovies can further be utilized as salted for shelf-life extension, particularly for the dry-salted products.
